title: Knowledge check: Building Reusable UI Systems

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Building Reusable UI Systems”?
options: Use create-vue with Vite for new Vue projects, understand the SFC/entry-point roles, and test production builds separately from the dev server.
Use Vue CLI as the primary new-project scaffolder without checking its status.
Edit generated dist assets as the source of truth.
Expose private credentials in client-side environment variables.
questions.answer_key: Use create-vue with Vite for new Vue projects, understand the SFC/entry-point roles, and test production builds separately from the dev server.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Building Reusable UI Systems directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “Shared components and design tokens”, which practice is most reliable?
options: Change every package at once without a rollback plan.
Legacy Vue 2 projects receive all current Vue 3 features automatically.
A project is maintainable when it has no setup documentation.
A safe migration begins with dependency/behavior inventory, tests, small reversible changes, and documentation.
questions.answer_key: A safe migration begins with dependency/behavior inventory, tests, small reversible changes, and documentation.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “Shared components and design tokens”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Building Reusable UI Systems” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.

review_note: Answer keys and explanations are server-side data. Human review required before publication.
